title: Anomalous Structures of Fisher Zero Lines in Biorthogonal Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: Wen-Hui Nie, Chong Li, Lin-Cheng Wang
abstract: Fisher zero lines of the Loschmidt amplitude in non-Hermitian quenches can exhibit anomalous structures in the complex time plane, such as divergence, separation, and the restriction of all branches or a specific branch to the real or imaginary axis. Here, we use the biorthogonal framework to reveal the origin of these structures and determine the corresponding critical momentum conditions by analyzing the values of $m_k=\hat{\mathbf{h}}_0\cdot\hat{\mathbf{h}}_1$, the dot product between the normalized prequench and postquench complex Bloch vectors. When Fisher zeros continuously cover the real-time axis, the density of Fisher zeros is further introduced to identify the critical times within these critical regions, at which the rate function becomes nonanalytic. We verify our results in a generalized non-Hermitian SSH model by quenching the Peierls phase and the non-Hermitian gain-loss strength, and also use the Jordan form to analyze the dynamics at postquench exceptional points, where the conventional Fisher zero formula is not applicable.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the complex structures of Fisher zero lines in non-Hermitian systems undergoing dynamical quantum phase transitions. By utilizing the biorthogonal framework, the authors determine critical momentum conditions based on the overlap of pre- and post-quench Bloch vectors. This provides a robust diagnostic tool for identifying nonanalyticities in the system's rate function.
main_problem: The paper investigates the anomalous structures of Fisher zero lines in the complex time plane associated with Biorthogonal Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions (DQPTs).
main_result: The anomalous structures of these zero lines, determined by the overlap parameter $m_k$, reveal the critical momentum conditions for DQPTs, even when standard formulas fail at exceptional points.
method: The analysis employs the biorthogonal framework to study the Loschmidt amplitude in the complex time plane, introducing the density of Fisher zeros to characterize nonanalyticities in the rate function.
model_or_system: The study is primarily based on non-Hermitian quenches, exemplified by a generalized non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model, analyzing the dynamics using Bloch vectors.
key_observables: Fisher zeros ($z_n$), the overlap parameter $m_k = \hat{\mathbf{h}}_0\cdot\hat{\mathbf{h}}_1$, and the rate function $\lambda(t)$ or its density $ho(t)$.
important_parameters: The overlap parameter $m_k$, the Peierls phase ($\phi$), and the non-Hermitian gain-loss strength ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the biorthogonal framework, and special care must be taken at exceptional points where the standard Fisher zero formula is inapplicable.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of $m_k$ on momentum $k$, the resulting complex trajectories of Fisher zeros $z_n(k)$, and the corresponding rate function $\lambda(t)$ or its density $ho(t)$ versus time or momentum.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the complex structure of the Fisher zeros based on the value of $m_k$ (real, purely imaginary, or complex), derives critical conditions from the real-time axis crossing, and verifies these findings using the SSH model and the Jordan form near exceptional points.
why_interesting: The connection between the geometry of zeros in the complex time plane and nonanalyticities in the rate function provides a powerful, general diagnostic tool for identifying non-equilibrium phase transitions in complex quantum systems.
